weekly.headline: AI agents meet their guardrails: identity, budgets and patch gaps
weekly.intro: A week in which the controls around AI coding agents — who they are, what they can spend, what they can touch — got more attention than the models themselves.

themes.title: Coding agents are now an endpoint security problem
themes.takeaway: Inventory which AI coding agents run on developer laptops and what they can reach, before a third-party installer silently reconfigures them for you.
themes.detail: A developer reported Postman's desktop app installing plugins into Claude Code and OpenAI Codex without consent. Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code for bankers, Palo Alto shipped a Cortex XDR integration for Claude Cowork desktop agents, and Docker joined a 12-company Blueprint Alliance reference architecture for securing agents.

articles.title: A developer opened Postman. Then two AI coding agents changed without their permission.
Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code for bankers — but made one surprising exception
New Cortex XDR Integration with Claude Cowork Secures Desktop AI Agents

themes.title: The patch gap is shrinking faster than your change window
themes.takeaway: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is outpacing enterprise remediation cycles, so compensating controls matter more than waiting for the next maintenance window.
themes.detail: OpenAI's autonomous pipeline found, validated and patched 948 local privilege-escalation bugs in the Linux kernel. Meanwhile two critical PHP flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619) triggered vendor advisories from Palo Alto and Cisco, and Red Hat pushed Lightwell dependency backports as an alternative to rushed major-version upgrades.

articles.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
Guiding Customers Through Critical PHP Vulnerabilities
Why Lightwell pairs dependency backports with upstream collaboration

themes.title: Token budgets replace unlimited agent compute
themes.takeaway: Budget agent inference like cloud spend this quarter: vendors are now capping, metering and pooling usage in ways that will interrupt running work.
themes.detail: Cognition added hierarchical budgets to Devin that can cut an agent off mid-task, OpenAI merged ChatGPT and Codex into a shared usage pool, and Anthropic removed the five-hour cap only for $200 Ultra accounts. Apple reportedly cut internal AI budgets and Musk throttled Grok Bot over "unsustainably high" costs.

articles.title: Your AI coding agent now runs on a budget — and it can cut you off mid-task

themes.title: Who signed this model response? Nobody knows yet
themes.takeaway: You currently cannot verify which model actually served an API call, which undermines audit trails for any regulated workload routed through a model gateway.
themes.detail: Anthropic's FlashProve would let callers cryptographically check that a response came from the claimed model, though the article flags a significant cost penalty. Separately Anthropic moved into identity, auto-connecting employees to approved Claude plugins via SSO rather than per-plugin logins.

themes.title: Memory shortage is now a hardware budget line
themes.takeaway: Factor RAM-driven price rises into 2027 refresh and capacity plans; AI datacentre demand is pulling memory away from servers and desktops alike.
